faculty.name: Dr. Arindam Banerjee
faculty.degrees: Ph.D. in Biomedical Instrumentation, M.Tech (IIT Kharagpur)
faculty.almaMater: Adamas University / Formerly Research Fellow at IISc
faculty.specialization: Biosensors, Non-Invasive Diagnostics, Neural Signal Processing
faculty.bio: Dr. Arindam Banerjee has over 18 years of academic and clinical research experience in biomedical signal processing and wearable biosensor systems. He leads the Center for Advanced Bio-Imaging & Sensing at Adamas University.
featuredPublications: Banerjee, A. et al. (2025). High-Resolution Wearable ECG Sensing Array for Early Arrhythmia Detection. IEEE Trans. Biomed. Eng.
Banerjee, A. & Roy, S. (2024). Wavelet-Based Denoising Algorithms for Ambulatory EEG Monitoring. Biosensors Journal.

faculty.name: Dr. Sunita Roy
faculty.degrees: Ph.D. in Biomaterials Engineering (NITH), M.S. (Calcutta Univ)
faculty.almaMater: Adamas University / Former Scientist at CSIR-CGCRI
faculty.specialization: Bioceramics, 3D Bioprinting Scaffolds, Controlled Drug Delivery
faculty.bio: Dr. Sunita Roy specializes in tissue scaffolding for orthopedic repair and bio-ink formulation for 3D bioprinting. She collaborates extensively with leading hospitals in Kolkata for clinical translational studies.
featuredPublications: Roy, S. et al. (2025). Chitosan-Hydroxyapatite Nanocomposite Scaffolds for Bone Regeneration. Biomaterials Science.
Roy, S. & Das, P. (2023). Injectable Hydrogels for Localized Chemotherapy Delivery. ACS Applied Bio Materials.

faculty.name: Dr. Bikramjit Das
faculty.degrees: Ph.D. in Computer Science & Medical AI, M.Tech (Jadavpur Univ)
faculty.specialization: Deep Learning in Radiology, Predictive Healthcare Analytics, Telemedicine
faculty.bio: Dr. Bikramjit Das pioneers research in vision transformers for chest X-ray and MRI segmentation. He directs the Healthcare AI & Neural Engineering Hub at the department.
featuredPublications: Das, B. et al. (2025). Transformer-Based Multi-Class Brain Tumor Segmentation from Multi-Modal MRI. Medical Image Analysis.
Das, B. & Mukhopadhyay, T. (2024). Edge-AI Architecture for Rural Tele-Diagnostic Screening. Healthcare Tech Letters.

faculty.name: Dr. Ananya Mukherjee
faculty.bio: Dr. Ananya Mukherjee develops low-cost microfluidic chips for rapid pathogen identification and blood biomarker quantification, aiming for rural point-of-care utility.
featuredPublications: Mukherjee, A. et al. (2024). Portable Microfluidic Chip for Rapid Sepsis Biomarker Detection. Biosensors & Bioelectronics.

faculty.name: Dr. Debasis Ghosh
faculty.specialization: Prosthetic Design, Implant Biomechanics, Motion Analysis
faculty.bio: Dr. Debasis Ghosh bridges biomechanical modeling with clinical rehabilitation. He works on patient-customized joint prostheses and gait biomechanics assessment.
featuredPublications: Ghosh, D. et al. (2025). Topology Optimization of Patient-Specific Hip Implants. Journal of Biomechanical Engineering.

faculty.name: Dr. Priya Sen
faculty.specialization: Electronic Health Records Mining, Wearable Biosignal Analytics, Rehabilitation AI
faculty.bio: Dr. Priya Sen leads research in intelligent rehabilitation games and wearable stroke-recovery monitors, working closely with clinical physical therapists.
featuredPublications: Sen, P. et al. (2024). Inertial Sensor Fusion for Quantitative Upper-Limb Rehabilitation. IEEE Trans. Neural Syst. Rehabil. Eng.

faculty.name: Prof. Sourav Chakraborty
faculty.degrees: M.Tech in Medical Electronics, 20+ Yrs Industry Experience
faculty.almaMater: Formerly Vice President R&D, Healthcare MedTech Devices
faculty.specialization: Medical Device Regulatory Standards (ISO 13485, US-FDA), Clinical Engineering
faculty.bio: Prof. Sourav Chakraborty brings 20 years of medical device commercialization experience to Adamas University, mentoring students in device prototyping, clinical trial protocol, and regulatory compliance.
featuredPublications: Chakraborty, S. (2023). Regulatory Strategy for AI-Enabled Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) in South Asia. Healthcare Regulation Standard.

faculty.name: Dr. Ritu Chatterji
faculty.bio: Dr. Ritu Chatterji researches antimicrobial nanocoatings for surgical implants and targeted drug carriers for oncological applications.
featuredPublications: Chatterji, R. et al. (2024). Silver Nanoparticle Functionalized Titanium Implants for Bacterial Biofilm Inhibition. Journal of Nanobiotechnology.

researchTracks.title: Biomedical Instrumentation & Signal Processing
researchTracks.subtitle: Biosensors, Medical Imaging, Diagnostic Systems & Electrophysiology
researchTracks.description: Focuses on designing next-generation electronic sensors, microfluidic chips, and advanced physiological signal processing algorithms. Researchers develop non-invasive diagnostic tools, wireless ECG/EEG monitoring systems, and optical biosensors for point-of-care disease screening.

researchTracks.title: Biomaterials & Tissue Engineering
researchTracks.subtitle: 3D Bioprinting, Regenerative Medicine, Implants & Drug Delivery
researchTracks.description: Combines polymer science, cell biology, and 3D printing technology to fabricate bio-inspired materials for damaged organ repair, bone defect fillers, and patient-tailored prosthetic implants. Includes targeted nanomedicine for localized drug release with minimal side effects.

researchTracks.title: Health Informatics & AI in Medicine
researchTracks.subtitle: Medical AI/ML, Telemedicine, Wearable Tech & Rehabilitation Robotics
researchTracks.description: Leverages artificial intelligence, computer vision, and IoT connectivity to build intelligent diagnostic assistants, tele-ICU monitoring infrastructure, wearable stroke recovery bands, and assistive exoskeletons for neuro-rehabilitation.

programs.title: B.Tech in Biomedical Engineering
programs.affiliation: School of Engineering & Technology, Adamas University | AICTE Approved
programs.shortDesc: A flagship 4-year undergraduate program combining fundamental engineering principles with biology, medical instrumentation, biomaterials, and clinical healthcare systems.
programs.fullDesc: The B.Tech in Biomedical Engineering at Adamas University equips students with deep interdisciplinary training in electronic instrumentation, human physiology, medical imaging, 3D bioprinting, and bio-AI. Students gain extensive hands-on experience in state-of-the-art department laboratories and undertake clinical internships at leading super-specialty hospitals in Kolkata.
highlights: Specialization Tracks in Bio-AI, Instrumentation, and Biomaterials
Hands-on Training with Medical Ultrasound, ECG/EEG, and 3D Bioprinters
Preparation for GATE, GRE, and Global Higher Studies
programs.eligibility: Passed 10+2 examination with Physics, Mathematics, and Chemistry/Biology/Computer Science with minimum 50% marks (45% for reserved category). Valid score in WBJEE / JEE Main / Adamas University Engineering Admission Test (AUAT).
careerOutcomes: Biomedical Equipment Engineer (Siemens, Philips, GE Healthcare)
Regulatory Affairs Specialist for Medical Devices
Graduate Studies (MS / M.Tech) in Top Global Universities

courses: Medical Imaging Systems (X-Ray, CT, MRI, Ultrasound)

testimonials.name: Subhashis Roy
testimonials.quote: The practical exposure in medical instrumentation labs at Adamas University gave me a massive head start. Working directly with ultrasound digitizers and patient monitors prepared me for real hospital deployments from day one.

testimonials.name: Dr. Sayani Dutta
testimonials.quote: Adamas provided an exceptional research atmosphere. Under Dr. Sunita Roy's guidance, my master's thesis on 3D bioprinted hydrogels led to two international journal publications and my PhD fellowship abroad.

testimonials.name: Rohan Bhattacharya
testimonials.quote: The integration of AI modules alongside core biomedical curriculum at Adamas SET is unmatched. I gained deep hands-on expertise in PyTorch and DICOM medical imaging analytics during my capstone project.
